source.text: מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֣נִי בַמִּדְבָּ֗ר מְלוֹן֙ אֹֽרְחִ֔ים וְאֶֽעֶזְבָה֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְאֵלְכָ֖ה מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of travelers, and I will leave my people and go from them; for all of them [are] adulterers, an assembly of treacherous [ones].

en.L: Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of travelers, \q that I may leave my people and go away from them! \q For all of them [are] adulterers, \q an assembly of treacherous [ones].
en.B: If only I had a travelers' shelter in the wilderness, \q so that I could leave my people and go far away from them! \q For they are all adulterers, \q a crowd of traitors.
en.R: I wish I had a place in the desert where travelers stop for the night. \q Then I could leave my people and get away from them. \q For they all commit adultery. \q They are a crowd of people who break faith.

es.L: ¡Quién me diera en el desierto un albergue de caminantes, \q para dejar a mi pueblo e irme lejos de ellos! \q Porque todos ellos [son] adúlteros, \q una asamblea de traidores.
es.B: ¡Ojalá tuviera en el desierto un refugio de viajeros, \q para poder dejar a mi pueblo e irme lejos de ellos! \q Porque todos son adúlteros, \q una banda de traidores.
es.R: Quisiera tener un lugar en el desierto donde los viajeros pasan la noche. \q Así podría dejar a mi pueblo y alejarme de ellos. \q Porque todos cometen adulterio. \q Son una banda de gente que no cumple su palabra.

fr.L: Qui me donnera dans le désert un gîte de voyageurs, \q pour que je quitte mon peuple et que je m’en aille loin d’eux ! \q Car tous [sont] des adultères, \q une bande de traîtres.
fr.B: Si seulement j’avais au désert un abri pour voyageurs, \q je pourrais quitter mon peuple et m’en aller loin d’eux ! \q Car ils sont tous adultères, \q une foule de traîtres.
fr.R: Je voudrais avoir dans le désert un endroit où les voyageurs s’arrêtent pour la nuit. \q Alors je pourrais quitter mon peuple et m’éloigner d’eux. \q Car ils commettent tous l’adultère. \q C’est une foule de gens qui trahissent.

sw.L: Laiti ningepewa nyikani mahali pa kulala pa wasafiri, \q ili niwaache watu wangu na kuondoka kwao! \q Kwa maana wote [ni] wazinzi, \q kusanyiko la wasaliti.
sw.B: Laiti ningekuwa na kibanda cha wasafiri nyikani, \q ili niwaache watu wangu na kwenda mbali nao! \q Kwa maana wote ni wazinzi, \q kundi la wasaliti.
sw.R: Natamani ningekuwa na mahali jangwani ambapo wasafiri hulala usiku. \q Ndipo ningeweza kuwaacha watu wangu na kwenda mbali nao. \q Kwa maana wote wanazini. \q Ni kundi la watu wasio waaminifu.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 9:1-25 is 9:2-26 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 8 ends with verse 23 ("Oh that my head were waters ..."), which many Bibles number 9:1, and so this verse and the rest of the chapter (9:1-25 here) are numbered 9:2-26 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ. Jeremiah is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: who will give me: a wish; the speaker is most likely the prophet, still grieving as in 8:23
decisions.reason: "Who will give me ...?" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "If only I had ...", the same words that open 8:23. There the prophet wishes he could weep day and night for his people; here he wishes he could get away from them. The poem gives no name, and from verse 2 on the LORD speaks ("they do not know me, declares the LORD"), so the wish may also be heard as God's own, weary of a people who betray him. Prophet and God grieve with one voice in these chapters.

decisions.choice: a lodging place of travelers: a bare overnight shelter on a desert route
decisions.reason: This was the simplest kind of stopping place on a road through empty country: a spot with shelter, perhaps water, where people on the move spent a night. Even that lonely place would be better than living among his own people.

decisions.choice: adulterers ... an assembly of treacherous: faithless to their marriages and to their God
decisions.reason: Jeremiah charges the people with real adultery (5:7-8; 7:9) and also uses marriage unfaithfulness as a picture of turning from God (3:8-9). The word for "assembly" usually means a solemn gathering for worship (Isaiah 1:13; Joel 1:14); here it is a gathering of people who break faith, which sharpens the charge.

decisions.choice: If only I had ... / I wish I had; a crowd of traitors / people who break faith
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Hebrew idiom of wishing ("who will give me") as a plain English wish. Readable says "commit adultery" and spells out "treacherous" as people who break faith.

decisions.choice: Hebrew numbering, 9:1
decisions.reason: As the English, the verses keep the Hebrew numbering: Hebrew 9:1-25 is 9:2-26 in Spanish Bibles that follow the Latin numbering, such as the Reina-Valera.

decisions.choice: Laiti (Literal, Balanced); Natamani (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wish "who will give me" is worded as in 8:23.

decisions.choice: Hebrew verse numbers kept (9:1 here is 9:2 in Bibles that follow the Latin)
decisions.reason: As the English, the French follows the Hebrew numbering throughout (see the meaning decision).

source.text: וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ אֶת־לְשׁוֹנָם֙ קַשְׁתָּ֣ם שֶׁ֔קֶר וְלֹ֥א לֶאֱמוּנָ֖ה גָּבְר֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ כִּי֩ מֵרָעָ֨ה אֶל־רָעָ֧ה׀יָצָ֛אוּ וְאֹתִ֥י לֹֽא־יָדָ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they bend their tongue, their bow, [of] falsehood, and not for faithfulness they are strong in the land; for from evil to evil they go out, and me they do not know, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And they bend their tongue, their bow, [for] falsehood, \q and not for faithfulness are they strong in the land; \q for from evil to evil they go out, and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they do not know, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies; \q they have grown strong in the land, but not by truth. \q For they go on from one evil to the next, and they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Their tongues are like bows, ready to shoot lies. \q They have become powerful in the land, but not by being honest. \q They go from one evil thing to another. They do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y tensan su lengua, su arco, [para] la mentira, \q y no por la fidelidad se han hecho fuertes en la tierra; \q porque de mal en mal salen, y a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Tensan su lengua como un arco para disparar mentiras; \q se han hecho fuertes en la tierra, pero no por la verdad. \q Porque van de un mal a otro, y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Su lengua es como un arco, lista para disparar mentiras. \q Se han hecho poderosos en el país, pero no por ser honrados. \q Van de una maldad a otra. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et ils tendent leur langue, leur arc, [pour] le mensonge, \q et ce n’est pas par la fidélité qu’ils sont forts dans le pays ; \q car ils vont de mal en mal, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissent pas, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ils tendent leur langue comme un arc pour tirer des mensonges ; \q ils sont devenus puissants dans le pays, mais pas par la vérité. \q Car ils vont d’un mal à l’autre, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissent pas, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Leurs langues sont comme des arcs prêts à tirer des mensonges. \q Ils sont devenus puissants dans le pays, mais pas en étant honnêtes. \q Ils vont d’un mal à l’autre. Ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissent pas, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nao wanapinda ulimi wao, upinde wao, [kwa] uongo, \q wala si kwa uaminifu wamekuwa hodari katika nchi; \q kwa maana wanatoka uovu hata uovu, wala {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hawanijui, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Wanapinda ndimi zao kama pinde ili kurusha uongo; \q wamepata nguvu katika nchi, lakini si kwa kweli. \q Kwa maana wanatoka uovu mmoja hadi mwingine, wala hawanijui, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ndimi zao ni kama pinde zilizo tayari kurusha uongo. \q Wamekuwa na nguvu katika nchi, lakini si kwa kuwa waaminifu. \q Wanatoka katika ubaya mmoja hadi mwingine. Hawanijui, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: they bend their tongue, their bow: the tongue is a bow drawn to shoot lies
decisions.reason: To "bend" a bow is to bend it to string it, ready to shoot. The Hebrew sets "their tongue" and "their bow" side by side: their tongue is their weapon, and its arrows are lies (verse 7; Psalm 64:4).

decisions.choice: not for faithfulness are they strong: their power in the land does not rest on truth
decisions.reason: The word means faithfulness, reliability, truth kept (5:1, 3; 7:28). They have become strong in the land, but not by faithfulness and not to serve it; their strength rests on lying.

decisions.choice: they do not know me: they do not acknowledge the LORD or live in his covenant
decisions.reason: To "know" the LORD is more than knowing about him: it is to acknowledge him and live faithfully toward him (Hosea 4:1, 6; Jeremiah 22:16). The charge returns in verse 5 and is answered in verse 23, where knowing the LORD is the one thing worth boasting of.

decisions.choice: like bows to shoot lies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "like" and "to shoot" to make the picture of the tongue as a bow clear (meaning decision m1).

source.text: אִ֤ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ הִשָּׁמֵ֔רוּ וְעַל־כָּל־אָ֖ח אַל־תִּבְטָ֑חוּ כִּ֤י כָל־אָח֙ עָק֣וֹב יַעְקֹ֔ב וְכָל־רֵ֖עַ רָכִ֥יל יַהֲלֹֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Each from his neighbor guard yourselves, and on any brother do not trust; for every brother supplanting supplants, and every neighbor [as a] slanderer goes about.

en.L: Each [of you], be on guard against your neighbor, \q and do not trust in any brother; \q for every brother surely supplants, \q and every neighbor goes about [as] a slanderer.
en.B: Be on guard, every one of you, against your neighbor, \q and put no trust in any brother. \q For every brother is a cheat like Jacob, \q and every neighbor goes around spreading slander.
en.R: Each of you, watch out for your neighbors. \q Do not trust even your own brother. \q For every brother cheats, as Jacob cheated his brother. \q Every neighbor goes around telling lies about others.

es.L: {{plural_you:Cuídense|Guardaos}} cada uno de su prójimo, \q y no {{plural_you:confíen|confiéis}} en ningún hermano; \q porque todo hermano suplanta sin falta, \q y todo prójimo anda calumniando.
es.B: {{plural_you:Cuídense|Guardaos}}, cada uno, de su prójimo, \q y no {{plural_you:confíen|confiéis}} en ningún hermano. \q Porque todo hermano es un tramposo como Jacob, \q y todo prójimo anda esparciendo calumnias.
es.R: Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:cuídese|cuidaos}} de sus vecinos. \q No {{plural_you:confíen|confiéis}} ni siquiera en su propio hermano. \q Porque todo hermano engaña, como Jacob engañó a su hermano. \q Todo vecino anda diciendo mentiras de los demás.

fr.L: Gardez-vous chacun de votre prochain, \q et ne vous fiez à aucun frère ; \q car tout frère ne fait que supplanter, \q et tout prochain va colportant la calomnie.
fr.B: Que chacun de vous se méfie de son prochain, \q et ne faites confiance à aucun frère. \q Car tout frère est un trompeur comme Jacob, \q et tout prochain s’en va répandre la calomnie.
fr.R: Que chacun de vous fasse attention à ses voisins. \q Ne faites même pas confiance à votre propre frère. \q Car chaque frère trompe, comme Jacob a trompé son frère. \q Chaque voisin va partout dire du mal des autres.

sw.L: Kila mmoja [wenu], jilindeni na jirani yake, \q wala msimtumaini ndugu yeyote; \q kwa maana kila ndugu hakika ni mwenye kuchukua nafasi ya mwenzake, \q na kila jirani anatembea [kama] msingiziaji.
sw.B: Jihadharini, kila mmoja wenu, na jirani yake, \q wala msimtumaini ndugu yeyote. \q Kwa maana kila ndugu ni mdanganyifu kama Yakobo, \q na kila jirani anazunguka akieneza masingizio.
sw.R: Kila mmoja wenu, jihadharini na majirani zenu. \q Msimwamini hata ndugu yenu mwenyewe. \q Kwa maana kila ndugu anadanganya, kama Yakobo alivyomdanganya ndugu yake. \q Kila jirani anazunguka akiwasingizia wengine.

decisions.choice: every brother surely supplants: a play on the name Jacob, who cheated his brother
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says, word for word, "every brother supplanting supplants" (*'aqov ya'qov*), and the second word is written with the same letters as the name Jacob (*ya'aqov*). The verb means to grab by the heel, to trip up from behind, to cheat someone out of what is theirs. Jacob was born holding his brother's heel (Genesis 25:26), and Esau said of him, "Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times" (Genesis 27:36; compare Hosea 12:4). Jeremiah says the people of Jacob have all become like their ancestor at his worst: every brother cheats his brother.

decisions.choice: every neighbor goes about as a slanderer: the words of the law in Leviticus 19:16
decisions.reason: The phrase "go about as a slanderer" is the one used in the law, "You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people" (Leviticus 19:16). The word means someone who carries tales from house to house, spreading gossip and false charges (6:28).

decisions.choice: neighbor ... brother: those closest to you, relatives and fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "Neighbor" is the person next to you, a friend or fellow citizen; "brother" is a relative or fellow Israelite. When even these cannot be trusted, the whole society has broken down (12:6; Micah 7:5-6).

decisions.choice: a cheat like Jacob / cheats, as Jacob cheated his brother
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, so that the reader hears the wordplay that the Hebrew carries in the verb itself (meaning decision m1). The name is not written in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "un tramposo como Jacob" (B); "como Jacob engañó a su hermano" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb plays on the name Jacob ('aqov ya'qov); Spanish cannot keep the sound, so Balanced and Readable name Jacob, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ni mwenye kuchukua nafasi ya mwenzake (Literal); ni mdanganyifu kama Yakobo (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb plays on Jacob's name (meaning decision m1); Literal gives its sense, "one who takes another's place", and Balanced and Readable name Jacob as the English does.

decisions.choice: "supplanter"
decisions.reason: "Supplanter" is the French word of Genesis 27:36 for Jacob, so Literal keeps the play on his name that Balanced and Readable spell out.

source.text: וְאִ֤ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ יְהָתֵ֔לּוּ וֶאֱמֶ֖ת לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ לִמְּד֧וּ לְשׁוֹנָ֛ם דַּבֶּר־שֶׁ֖קֶר הַעֲוֵ֥ה נִלְאֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And each [one] his neighbor they deceive, and truth they do not speak; they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood; to do iniquity they weary themselves.

en.L: And each one deceives {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q and they do not speak truth; \q they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood; they weary themselves doing iniquity.
en.B: Everyone cheats {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q and no one speaks the truth. \q They have trained their tongues to tell lies; they wear themselves out doing wrong.
en.R: They all cheat one another. \q No one tells the truth. \q They have taught themselves to lie, and they work so hard at doing wrong that they wear themselves out.

es.L: Y cada uno engaña a su prójimo, \q y no hablan verdad; \q han enseñado a su lengua a hablar mentira; se cansan de hacer iniquidad.
es.B: Cada uno engaña a su prójimo, \q y nadie dice la verdad. \q Han entrenado su lengua para decir mentiras; se agotan haciendo el mal.
es.R: Todos se engañan unos a otros. \q Nadie dice la verdad. \q Se han enseñado a mentir, y se esfuerzan tanto en hacer el mal que se agotan.

fr.L: Et chacun trompe son prochain, \q et ils ne disent pas la vérité ; \q ils ont appris à leur langue à dire le mensonge ; ils se fatiguent à commettre la faute.
fr.B: Chacun dupe son prochain, \q et personne ne dit la vérité. \q Ils ont exercé leur langue au mensonge ; ils s’épuisent à mal faire.
fr.R: Ils se trompent tous les uns les autres. \q Personne ne dit la vérité. \q Ils se sont habitués à mentir, et ils se donnent tant de mal pour faire le mal qu’ils s’en épuisent.

sw.L: Na kila mmoja anamdanganya jirani yake, \q wala hawasemi kweli; \q wamefundisha ndimi zao kusema uongo; wanajichosha kwa kutenda uovu.
sw.B: Kila mtu anamdanganya jirani yake, \q wala hakuna anayesema kweli. \q Wamezizoeza ndimi zao kusema uongo; wanajichosha kwa kutenda mabaya.
sw.R: Wote wanadanganyana. \q Hakuna anayesema ukweli. \q Wamejifundisha kusema uongo, nao wanajitahidi sana kutenda mabaya hata wanachoka.

decisions.choice: deceives: cheats, makes a fool of
decisions.reason: The verb means to trifle with someone, to mock or cheat them. Jacob used it of Laban: "your father has cheated me" (Genesis 31:7), so the picture of verse 3 goes on.

decisions.choice: they weary themselves doing iniquity: they exhaust themselves in wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Doing wrong has become hard work that they pursue until they are worn out. They put more effort into sin than it would take to do right.

decisions.choice: taught themselves to lie; work so hard ... that they wear themselves out
decisions.reason: Readable says "taught themselves" for "taught their tongue" and spells out what it means to weary oneself in wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: "su prójimo", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" and "cada uno" serve for men and women alike, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart here or in verse 7.

source.text: שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ בְּת֣וֹךְ מִרְמָ֑ה בְּמִרְמָ֛ה מֵאֲנ֥וּ דַֽעַת־אוֹתִ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Your dwelling [is] in [the] midst of deceit; in deceit they refuse to know me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Your dwelling [is] in the midst of deceit; \q in deceit they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You live surrounded by deceit; \q in their deceit they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You live among people who lie and cheat. \q They are so full of lies that they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Tu morada [está] en medio del engaño; \q por el engaño rehúsan conocer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Vives rodeado de engaño; \q en su engaño se niegan a conocer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Vives entre gente que miente y engaña. \q Están tan llenos de mentiras que se niegan a conocer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Ta demeure [est] au milieu de la tromperie ; \q dans la tromperie ils refusent de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Tu habites au milieu de la tromperie ; \q dans leur tromperie, ils refusent de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Tu vis au milieu de gens qui mentent et qui trichent. \q Ils sont si pleins de mensonges qu’ils refusent de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Makao yako [yako] katikati ya udanganyifu; \q kwa udanganyifu wanakataa kunijua, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Unaishi umezungukwa na udanganyifu; \q katika udanganyifu wao wanakataa kunijua, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Unaishi kati ya watu wanaosema uongo na kudanganya. \q Wamejaa uongo kiasi kwamba wanakataa kunijua, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: your dwelling: the LORD speaks to the prophet
decisions.reason: "Your" is singular. The LORD turns to Jeremiah, who had wished to get away from his people (verse 1): he lives in the middle of a deceitful people.

decisions.choice: in the midst of deceit; in deceit: the Hebrew text as written
alternatives: oppression upon oppression, deceit upon deceit
decisions.reason: The consonants of this line can also be divided into different words, giving "oppression upon oppression, deceit upon deceit; they refuse to know me". The Greek translation reads something like that. The Hebrew as it stands makes good sense: Jeremiah lives among deceit, and deceit is why they refuse to know the LORD.

decisions.choice: They are so full of lies that they refuse
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link between deceit and their refusal explicit, which the Hebrew "in deceit" implies.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י צוֹרְפָ֖ם וּבְחַנְתִּ֑ים כִּֽי־אֵ֣יךְ אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts: here I [am] refining them, and I will test them; for how shall I act because of [the] daughter of my people?

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q See, I am refining them, and I will test them; \q for how [else] shall I act because of the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people?
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q I am going to refine them and put them to the test, \q for how else can I deal with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear people?
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q I am going to put them through fire to make them pure, and I will test them. \q What else can I do, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have sinned like this?

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: \q He aquí que yo los refinaré y los probaré; \q porque ¿qué [otra cosa] haré por causa de la hija de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo?
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: \q Voy a refinarlos y a ponerlos a prueba, \q porque ¿de qué otra manera puedo tratar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} querido pueblo?
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: \q Voy a pasarlos por el fuego para purificarlos, y los pondré a prueba. \q ¿Qué otra cosa puedo hacer, cuando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo ha pecado así?

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : \q Voici, je vais les épurer et les éprouver ; \q car comment [autrement] agirais-je envers la fille de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ?
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : \q Je vais les épurer et les mettre à l’épreuve, \q car que puis-je faire d’autre avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cher peuple ?
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : \q Je vais les faire passer par le feu pour les rendre purs, et je vais les mettre à l’épreuve. \q Que puis-je faire d’autre, quand {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a péché ainsi ?

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: \q Tazama, nitawasafisha kama madini, nami nitawajaribu; \q kwa maana nifanye [nini tena] kwa sababu ya binti wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}?
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: \q Karibu nitawasafisha kama madini na kuwajaribu, \q kwa maana nifanye nini kingine kwa ajili ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wapendwa?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: \q Nitawapitisha motoni ili kuwatakasa, nami nitawajaribu. \q Nifanye nini kingine, watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wanapotenda dhambi namna hii?

decisions.choice: refining and testing: heating metal to separate the pure from the waste
decisions.reason: A metalworker melted silver or gold in a furnace so that the waste (dross) separated from it, and tested the result. God will put his people through suffering to purge them. Jeremiah had already been told that the refining of this people was in vain, because the wicked are not removed (6:27-30).

decisions.choice: how shall I act because of the daughter of my people: a question that means there is nothing else to do
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer: given what his people have become, the LORD has no other course. The Greek translation reads "because of the evil of the daughter of my people", saying outright what the Hebrew leaves implied.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: a tender name for the people
decisions.reason: As at its first use in Jeremiah, "daughter of my people" speaks of the people as a beloved daughter; it carries love and grief, not contempt (8:21-23).

decisions.choice: put them through fire to make them pure; when my people have sinned like this
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of refining and says what "because of" points to: the people's sin (meaning decision m2).

source.text: חֵ֥ץ שָׁח֛וּט לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם מִרְמָ֣ה דִבֵּ֑ר בְּפִ֗יו שָׁל֤וֹם אֶת־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ יְדַבֵּ֔רוּבְקִרְבּ֖וֹ יָשִׂ֥ים אָרְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: An arrow sharpened [is] their tongue; deceit it speaks; with his mouth peace with his neighbor he speaks, and in his inside he sets his ambush.

en.L: Their tongue [is] a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit; \q with {{gender:their|his}} mouth one speaks peace to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q but inwardly {{gender:they set their|he sets his}} ambush.
en.B: Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. \q With their mouths they speak peace to their neighbors, \q but in their hearts they set an ambush for them.
en.R: Their tongues are like sharp arrows. They tell lies. \q They speak words of peace to their neighbors, \q but inside they are planning to trap them.

es.L: Saeta afilada [es] su lengua; habla engaño; \q con su boca habla paz a su prójimo, \q pero por dentro le tiende emboscada.
es.B: Su lengua es una flecha afilada; habla engaño. \q Con la boca hablan de paz a sus vecinos, \q pero en su corazón les tienden una emboscada.
es.R: Su lengua es como una flecha afilada. Dicen mentiras. \q Les dicen palabras de paz a sus vecinos, \q pero por dentro están planeando atraparlos.

fr.L: Leur langue [est] une flèche aiguisée ; elle dit la tromperie ; \q de sa bouche on parle de paix avec son prochain, \q mais au-dedans de soi on lui dresse une embuscade.
fr.B: Leur langue est une flèche aiguisée ; elle dit la tromperie. \q De leur bouche, ils parlent de paix à leur prochain, \q mais dans leur cœur ils lui tendent un piège.
fr.R: Leurs langues sont comme des flèches pointues. Elles disent des mensonges. \q Ils parlent de paix à leurs voisins, \q mais au fond d’eux-mêmes, ils préparent un piège contre eux.

sw.L: Ulimi wao [ni] mshale ulionolewa; unasema udanganyifu; \q kwa kinywa chake mtu anasema amani na jirani yake, \q lakini ndani yake anamwekea mtego.
sw.B: Ulimi wao ni mshale ulionolewa; unasema udanganyifu. \q Kwa vinywa vyao wanawaambia jirani zao maneno ya amani, \q lakini mioyoni mwao wanawawekea mtego.
sw.R: Ndimi zao ni kama mishale mikali. Zinasema uongo. \q Wanawaambia jirani zao maneno ya amani, \q lakini ndani yao wanapanga kuwatega.

decisions.choice: a sharpened arrow: the reading of the Hebrew margin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as written has "a slaughtering arrow", a deadly arrow; the reading given in the margin, which this translation follows, has a word meaning "hammered" or "sharpened", used of beaten gold in 1 Kings 10:16-17. Either way the tongue is a weapon that kills.

decisions.choice: speaks peace: gives friendly greetings
decisions.reason: To "speak peace" with someone is to greet them warmly and wish them well (Psalm 28:3). The friendly words hide a plan to harm.

decisions.choice: in his inside he sets his ambush: inwardly he lies in wait
decisions.reason: An ambush is a hidden trap for an enemy (Joshua 8:2). The deceiver's heart is the hiding place where he waits for the moment to strike the neighbor he greets.

decisions.choice: plural: they speak ... their neighbors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from "their tongue" to a single representative person ("his mouth", "his neighbor"). Balanced and Readable keep the plural throughout, which says the same thing about everyone.

decisions.choice: kinywa chake ... jirani yake (no gender span)
decisions.reason: Swahili "chake" and "yake" are his or her alike, so the English gender spans have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "on ... son prochain ... soi", no gender span
decisions.reason: French generic "on" says "anyone" without choosing a gender, so the Literal needs none of the English gender spans.

source.text: הַעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא־אֶפְקָד־בָּ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה אִ֚ם בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For these [things] shall I not punish them, declares Yahweh? Or on a nation which [is] like this shall not my soul avenge itself?

en.L: Shall I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Or on a nation such as this \q shall not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul avenge itself?
en.B: Should I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q On a nation such as this \q should I not take vengeance?
en.R: Should I not punish them for doing these things? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Should I not pay back a nation like this?

es.L: ¿No he de castigarlos por estas cosas?, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q ¿O de una nación como esta \q no se vengará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alma?
es.B: ¿No debería castigarlos por estas cosas?, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q ¿No debería vengarme \q de una nación como esta?
es.R: ¿No debería castigarlos por hacer estas cosas?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q ¿No debería darle su merecido a una nación como esta?

fr.L: Ne les punirais-je pas pour ces choses ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Et d’une nation comme celle-ci \q {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} âme ne se vengerait-elle pas ?
fr.B: Ne devrais-je pas les punir pour cela ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q D’une nation comme celle-ci, \q ne devrais-je pas me venger ?
fr.R: Ne devrais-je pas les punir pour ce qu’ils font ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Ne devrais-je pas faire payer une nation comme celle-ci ?

sw.L: Je, nisiwaadhibu kwa ajili ya mambo haya? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Au juu ya taifa kama hili \q nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} isijilipizie kisasi?
sw.B: Je, nisiwaadhibu kwa ajili ya mambo haya? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Juu ya taifa kama hili \q nisilipize kisasi?
sw.R: Je, nisiwaadhibu kwa kutenda mambo haya? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Je, nisililipize taifa kama hili?

decisions.choice: the same refrain as 5:9 and 5:29
decisions.reason: These words repeat almost exactly the question of 5:9 and 5:29. Each time it ends a list of the people's wrongs: can the LORD let such things go?

decisions.choice: punish ... avenge itself: the rightful judge gives what is due
decisions.reason: The verb for "punish" means to visit, to come and deal with someone. To "avenge" here is not spite but the just answer of the rightful judge to wrongs done (Deuteronomy 32:35). "My soul" means "I myself".

decisions.choice: take vengeance / pay back, as in 5:9
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in 5:9 and 5:29 at every level (m1). Balanced and Readable say "take vengeance" and "pay back" for "my soul avenge itself", which is not natural English.

decisions.choice: the wording of 5:9 and 5:29 at each level
decisions.reason: The refrain repeats 5:9 and 5:29.

source.text: עַל־הֶ֨הָרִ֜ים אֶשָּׂ֧א בְכִ֣י וָנֶ֗הִי וְעַל־נְא֤וֹת מִדְבָּר֙ קִינָ֔ה כִּ֤י נִצְּתוּ֙ מִבְּלִי־אִ֣ישׁ עֹבֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ק֣וֹל מִקְנֶ֑ה מֵע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֔ה נָדְד֖וּ הָלָֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and for [the] pastures of [the] wilderness a lament, for they are burned without anyone passing through, and they do not hear [the] sound of livestock; from [the] bird of the heavens and to [the] beast they have fled, they have gone.

en.L: For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and for the pastures of the wilderness a lament, \q for they are burned, with no one passing through, \q and they do not hear the sound of livestock; \q from the birds of the heavens to the beasts, \q they have fled, they are gone.
en.B: I will weep and wail for the mountains, and raise a lament for the pastures in the wilderness, \q because they are scorched and no one travels through them, \q and no one hears the lowing of cattle. \q The birds of the sky and the animals \q have all fled and are gone.
en.R: I will cry and mourn for the mountains. \q I will sing a sad song for the grasslands in the wild country. \q They are burned up, and no one travels through them. \q No one hears cattle mooing there. \q The birds and the animals have all run away.

es.L: Por los montes alzaré llanto y gemido, y por los pastos del desierto un lamento, \q porque están quemados, sin que nadie pase, \q y no se oye el mugido del ganado; \q desde las aves del cielo hasta las bestias, \q huyeron, se fueron.
es.B: Lloraré y gemiré por los montes, y entonaré un lamento por los pastos del desierto, \q porque están abrasados y nadie pasa por ellos, \q y nadie oye el mugido del ganado. \q Las aves del cielo y los animales \q han huido todos y se han ido.
es.R: Lloraré y haré duelo por los montes. \q Cantaré un canto triste por los pastizales del campo abierto. \q Están quemados, y nadie pasa por ellos. \q Nadie oye allí mugir al ganado. \q Las aves y los animales se han ido todos.

fr.L: Sur les montagnes j’élèverai des pleurs et des gémissements, et sur les pâturages du désert une lamentation, \q car ils sont brûlés, personne n’y passe, \q et on n’y entend plus la voix du bétail ; \q depuis les oiseaux du ciel jusqu’aux bêtes, \q ils ont fui, ils sont partis.
fr.B: Je pleurerai et je gémirai sur les montagnes, j’entonnerai une lamentation sur les pâturages du désert, \q car ils sont brûlés et personne n’y passe, \q et on n’y entend plus le mugissement des troupeaux. \q Les oiseaux du ciel et les bêtes \q ont tous fui, ils ont disparu.
fr.R: Je vais pleurer et me lamenter sur les montagnes. \q Je vais chanter un chant de deuil sur les prairies de la campagne sauvage. \q Elles sont brûlées, et personne n’y passe plus. \q On n’y entend plus les vaches meugler. \q Les oiseaux et les animaux se sont tous enfuis.

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya milima nitaanza kulia na kuomboleza, na kwa ajili ya malisho ya nyikani maombolezo, \q kwa maana yameteketezwa, hakuna mtu apitaye, \q wala hawasikii sauti ya mifugo; \q tangu ndege wa angani hata mnyama, \q wamekimbia, wametoweka.
sw.B: Nitalia na kuomboleza kwa ajili ya milima, na kupaza maombolezo kwa ajili ya malisho ya nyikani, \q kwa sababu yameteketezwa na hakuna mtu anayepita huko, \q wala hakuna anayesikia mlio wa ng'ombe. \q Ndege wa angani na wanyama \q wote wamekimbia na kutoweka.
sw.R: Nitalia na kuomboleza kwa ajili ya milima. \q Nitaimba wimbo wa huzuni kwa ajili ya mbuga za nyikani. \q Zimeteketea, wala hakuna mtu anayepita humo. \q Hakuna anayesikia ng'ombe wakilia huko. \q Ndege na wanyama wote wamekimbia.

decisions.choice: I will take up: the speaker weeps for the land
alternatives: Take up weeping (a command to the people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will take up", and does not say whether the prophet or the LORD is weeping; the LORD speaks in verse 10. The Greek translation reads a plural command, "Take up weeping".

decisions.choice: burned: scorched, laid waste
decisions.reason: The verb means to be burned or set on fire. A similar verb in verse 11 means "laid waste", and the two pictures meet: the land is a burned-out waste where no one passes.

decisions.choice: pastures of the wilderness: open grazing land
decisions.reason: The "wilderness" here is not sand desert but open country beyond the farms, where flocks and herds grazed (23:10; Psalm 65:13). Even the animals and birds have left it.

decisions.choice: sing a sad song; grasslands in the wild country; cattle mooing
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "lament", "pastures of the wilderness" and "the sound of livestock".

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לְגַלִּ֖ים מְע֣וֹן תַּנִּ֑ים וְאֶת־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה אֶתֵּ֥ן שְׁמָמָ֖ה מִבְּלִ֖י יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make Jerusalem into heaps, a lair of jackals, and [the] cities of Judah I will make a desolation without inhabitant.

en.L: And I will make Jerusalem into heaps, a den of jackals, \q and the cities of Judah I will make a desolation without inhabitant.
en.B: I will turn Jerusalem into a heap of ruins, a den for jackals, \q and I will make the towns of Judah a wasteland where no one lives.
en.R: I will turn Jerusalem into piles of stones where jackals live. \q I will make the towns of Judah empty ruins where no one lives.

es.L: Y haré de Jerusalén montones [de ruinas], guarida de chacales, \q y de las ciudades de Judá haré una desolación sin habitante.
es.B: Convertiré a Jerusalén en un montón de ruinas, en una guarida de chacales, \q y haré de las ciudades de Judá un desierto donde nadie vive.
es.R: Convertiré a Jerusalén en montones de piedras donde viven los chacales. \q Haré de los pueblos de Judá ruinas vacías donde nadie vive.

fr.L: Et je ferai de Jérusalem des monceaux de pierres, un repaire de chacals, \q et des villes de Juda je ferai une désolation sans habitant.
fr.B: Je ferai de Jérusalem un tas de ruines, un repaire de chacals, \q et je ferai des villes de Juda un désert où personne n’habite.
fr.R: Je ferai de Jérusalem des tas de pierres où vivront les chacals. \q Je ferai des villes de Juda des ruines vides où personne n’habite.

sw.L: Nami nitaifanya Yerusalemu kuwa magofu, makao ya mbweha, \q na miji ya Yuda nitaifanya ukiwa bila mkaaji.
sw.B: Nitaigeuza Yerusalemu kuwa rundo la magofu, pango la mbweha, \q nami nitaifanya miji ya Yuda kuwa jangwa ambamo hakuna anayeishi.
sw.R: Nitaigeuza Yerusalemu kuwa marundo ya mawe ambako mbweha wanaishi. \q Nitaifanya miji ya Yuda kuwa magofu matupu ambamo hakuna anayeishi.

decisions.choice: I will make: the LORD now speaks
decisions.reason: The "I" of this verse is the LORD, who brings the ruin that verse 9 mourns.

decisions.choice: heaps, a den of jackals: a city turned to rubble where wild animals live
decisions.reason: "Heaps" are piles of stones from fallen buildings. Jackals, wild dogs that live in packs, make their dens in ruins far from people; to call a city their home is to say no one lives there any more (10:22; 49:33; Isaiah 34:13).

decisions.choice: towns of Judah
decisions.reason: The word covers walled places of every size; Balanced and Readable say "towns" for the many smaller places of Judah, as English usually does.

source.text: מִֽי־הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ וְיָבֵ֣ן אֶת־זֹ֔את וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר פִּֽי־יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו וְיַגִּדָ֑הּ עַל־מָה֙ אָבְדָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ נִצְּתָ֥ה כַמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִבְּלִ֖י עֹבֵֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] the man, the wise, and he will understand this, and [the one] whom [the] mouth of Yahweh has spoken to him, and he may declare it? For what has perished the land, [is it] laid waste like the wilderness without [one] passing through?

en.L: Who [is] {{gender:the wise one|the wise man}}, that {{gender:they|he}} may understand this? \q And to whom has the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken, that {{gender:they|he}} may declare it? \q Why has the land perished, \q laid waste like the wilderness, with no one passing through?
en.B: Who is wise enough to understand this? \q To whom has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken, so that {{gender:they|he}} can explain it? \q Why has the land been ruined \q and laid waste like a wilderness that no one crosses?
en.R: Who is wise enough to understand this? \q Who has heard from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and can explain it? \q Why has the land been ruined? \q Why has it become an empty waste like a desert, where no one travels?

es.L: ¿Quién [es] el sabio que entienda esto? \q ¿Y a quién ha hablado la boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que lo declare? \q ¿Por qué ha perecido la tierra, \q asolada como el desierto, sin que nadie pase?
es.B: ¿Quién es lo bastante sabio para entender esto? \q ¿A quién ha hablado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, para que pueda explicarlo? \q ¿Por qué ha sido arruinada la tierra \q y asolada como un desierto que nadie cruza?
es.R: ¿Quién es lo bastante sabio para entender esto? \q ¿Quién ha oído {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y puede explicarlo? \q ¿Por qué ha sido arruinada la tierra? \q ¿Por qué se ha convertido en un lugar vacío como un desierto, por donde nadie pasa?

fr.L: Qui [est] le sage qui comprendra cela ? \q Et à qui la bouche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a-t-elle parlé, pour qu’il l’annonce ? \q Pourquoi le pays a-t-il péri, \q dévasté comme le désert, sans personne qui y passe ?
fr.B: Qui est assez sage pour comprendre cela ? \q À qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il parlé, pour qu’il puisse l’expliquer ? \q Pourquoi le pays est-il ruiné \q et dévasté comme un désert que personne ne traverse ?
fr.R: Qui est assez sage pour comprendre cela ? \q Qui a entendu {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et peut l’expliquer ? \q Pourquoi le pays est-il ruiné ? \q Pourquoi est-il devenu vide comme un désert, où personne ne passe ?

sw.L: Ni nani mwenye hekima, apate kuelewa hili? \q Na ni nani ambaye kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kimesema naye, apate kulitangaza? \q Mbona nchi imeangamia, \q imeharibiwa kama nyika, bila mtu apitaye?
sw.B: Ni nani mwenye hekima ya kutosha kuelewa hili? \q Ni nani ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema naye, ili aweze kulieleza? \q Mbona nchi imeangamia \q na kuharibiwa kama nyika ambayo hakuna anayeivuka?
sw.R: Ni nani mwenye hekima ya kutosha kuelewa jambo hili? \q Ni nani aliyesikia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na anaweza kulieleza? \q Kwa nini nchi imeharibiwa? \q Kwa nini imekuwa tupu kama jangwa, ambako hakuna mtu anayesafiri?

decisions.choice: who ... why: questions that only the LORD can answer
decisions.reason: No wise person steps forward. The questions show that human wisdom cannot explain the ruin; the answer comes in verse 12 from the LORD himself. The wise man here prepares for verse 22, where the wise are told not to boast in their wisdom.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the LORD has spoken: the LORD himself has spoken
decisions.reason: "The mouth of the LORD" stresses that the words come directly from God (Isaiah 1:20; 40:5). Only someone the LORD has spoken to can declare why the land lies in ruins.

decisions.choice: Who is wise enough to understand this?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "Who is the wise man, that he may understand this?" as a single natural question with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: "el sabio", "lo declare", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "el sabio" and the verbs serve for anyone, man or woman, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart here.

decisions.choice: mwenye hekima ... apate (no gender span)
decisions.reason: "Mwenye hekima" and the verb prefix "a-" speak of a man or a woman alike, so the English gender spans have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "le sage", "à qui ... pour qu’il", no gender span
decisions.reason: French "le sage" and the "il" that refers back to "qui" are generic, as the style guide sets for "celui qui ... il", so the English gender spans have no French counterpart.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־עָזְבָם֙ אֶת־תּ֣וֹרָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֥וּ בְקוֹלִ֖י וְלֹא־הָ֥לְכוּ בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh: because they have forsaken my instruction which I set before them, and not they have listened to my voice and not walked in it,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: \q Because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, which I set before them, \q and have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, and have not walked in it,
en.B: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered: \q It is because they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, which I set before them; \q they have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice or followed it,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered: \q It is because they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching, which I gave them. \q They have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or lived by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: \q Porque abandonaron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción, que puse delante de ellos, \q y no escucharon {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, ni anduvieron en ella,
es.B: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: \q Es porque han abandonado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción, que puse delante de ellos; \q no han obedecido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz ni la han seguido,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: \q Es porque se han apartado de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza, que yo les di. \q No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han obedecido ni han vivido según {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : \q C’est parce qu’ils ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} loi, que j’avais mise devant eux, \q et qu’ils n’ont pas écouté {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix et n’ont pas marché selon elle,
fr.B: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répond : \q C’est parce qu’ils ont abandonné {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} instruction, que j’avais placée devant eux ; \q ils n’ont pas obéi à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix et ne l’ont pas suivie,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répond : \q C’est parce qu’ils se sont détournés de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} enseignement, que je leur avais donné. \q Ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont pas obéi et n’ont pas vécu selon {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} enseignement.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema: \q Kwa sababu wameiacha sheria {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} niliyoiweka mbele yao, \q wala hawakuisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, wala hawakuenenda ndani yake,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu: \q Ni kwa sababu wameyaacha mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} niliyoyaweka mbele yao; \q hawakuitii sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wala kuyafuata,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu: \q Ni kwa sababu wameyaacha mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} niliyowapa. \q Hawakunitii wala hawakuishi kwa kufuata mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: my instruction: the LORD's teaching for his people's life
decisions.reason: The word (*torah*) means instruction or teaching. It includes the laws given through Moses, but its sense is wider: all the LORD has taught his people about how to live with him (2:8; 8:8).

decisions.choice: listened to my voice ... walked in it: obeyed and lived by it
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone is to obey them; to "walk in" an instruction is to live by it day by day (7:23; 26:4).

decisions.choice: the LORD said: the answer to the questions of verse 11
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the question no wise person could. His answer runs through verses 12-13 and leads to the sentence in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "answered" for "said", because the LORD is replying to the questions of verse 11 (meaning decision m3). Readable also says "obeyed me" for "listened to my voice" and repeats "my teaching" to make clear what "it" refers to.

decisions.choice: "répond" (present)
decisions.reason: The LORD's answer is part of the poem, not narrative prose, so French keeps the tense of speech; Literal keeps the plain "dit".

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֑ם וְאַחֲרֵי֙ הַבְּעָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִמְּד֖וּם אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they have walked after [the] stubbornness of their heart and after the Baals, which their fathers taught them.

en.L: and they have walked after the stubbornness of their heart \q and after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.
en.B: but have followed the stubbornness of their own hearts \q and gone after the Baals, as their ancestors taught them.
en.R: Instead, they have stubbornly followed their own hearts. \q They have followed the Baals, false gods called Baal, just as their ancestors taught them.

es.L: sino que anduvieron tras la terquedad de su corazón \q y tras los baales, como les enseñaron sus padres.
es.B: sino que han seguido la terquedad de su propio corazón \q y han ido tras los baales, como les enseñaron sus antepasados.
es.R: Al contrario, han seguido con terquedad los deseos de su propio corazón. \q Han seguido a los baales, los dioses falsos llamados Baal, tal como les enseñaron sus antepasados.

fr.L: et ils ont marché selon l’obstination de leur cœur \q et derrière les Baals, comme leurs pères le leur ont appris.
fr.B: mais ils ont suivi l’obstination de leur cœur \q et sont allés derrière les Baals, comme leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} le leur ont appris.
fr.R: Au contraire, ils ont suivi avec obstination leur propre cœur. \q Ils ont suivi les Baals, les faux dieux appelés Baal, comme leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} le leur ont appris.

sw.L: bali wameufuata ukaidi wa moyo wao, \q na kuwafuata Mabaali, kama baba zao walivyowafundisha.
sw.B: bali wameufuata ukaidi wa mioyo yao wenyewe \q na kuwafuata Mabaali, kama babu zao walivyowafundisha.
sw.R: Badala yake, wamefuata kwa ukaidi mioyo yao wenyewe. \q Wamewafuata Mabaali, miungu ya uongo iitwayo Baali, kama vile babu zao walivyowafundisha.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their heart: doing what they themselves want, against God
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 29:18, of the person who says "I will be safe though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart", and Jeremiah uses it often (3:17; 7:24; 11:8). The heart is the seat of the will; they follow their own will instead of the LORD's voice. Here the word "evil", which the phrase has in some places, is not used.

decisions.choice: the Baals: the many local forms of the god Baal
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god, worshiped as the giver of rain and crops. He was honored at many local shrines under different titles, so the Bible often speaks of "the Baals" in the plural (2:23; Judges 2:11).

decisions.choice: as their fathers taught them: idolatry handed down from earlier generations
decisions.reason: The relative word can mean "which" (the Baals, which their fathers taught them about) or "as". Either way the worship of Baal was something learned from parents and grandparents (7:18; 16:11-12).

decisions.choice: followed; ancestors; the Baals, false gods called Baal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "followed" for "walked after" and "ancestors" for "fathers", which here means earlier generations. Readable explains who the Baals were, as this book does elsewhere.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֧י מַאֲכִילָ֛ם אֶת־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה לַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְהִשְׁקִיתִ֖ים מֵי־רֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: here I [am] feeding them, this people, wormwood, and I will give them to drink water of poison.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: \q See, I am feeding them, this people, wormwood, \q and I will give them poisoned water to drink.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: \q I am going to feed this people bitter wormwood \q and give them poisoned water to drink.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: \q I am going to give these people bitter plants to eat \q and poisoned water to drink.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: \q He aquí que yo les daré a comer, a este pueblo, ajenjo, \q y les daré a beber agua envenenada.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: \q Voy a dar a comer a este pueblo amargo ajenjo \q y les daré a beber agua envenenada.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: \q Voy a darle a esta gente plantas amargas para comer \q y agua envenenada para beber.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : \q Voici, je vais les nourrir, ce peuple, d’absinthe, \q et je leur ferai boire de l’eau empoisonnée.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : \q Je vais nourrir ce peuple d’absinthe amère \q et lui faire boire de l’eau empoisonnée.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : \q Je vais donner à ce peuple des plantes amères à manger \q et de l’eau empoisonnée à boire.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: \q Tazama, nitawalisha mchungu, watu hawa, \q nami nitawanywesha maji yenye sumu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: \q Karibu nitawalisha watu hawa mchungu wenye uchungu \q na kuwanywesha maji yenye sumu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: \q Nitawapa watu hawa mimea michungu wale \q na maji yenye sumu wanywe.

decisions.choice: wormwood ... poison: a bitter plant and a poisonous one
decisions.reason: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste (Amos 5:7; Lamentations 3:15, 19). The word joined to "water" names a poisonous plant, perhaps the poppy or hemlock; the exact plant is not known. Together they picture suffering that is bitter and deadly.

decisions.choice: wormwood and poison: the warning of Deuteronomy 29:17
decisions.reason: Moses warned that anyone who turned from the LORD to other gods would be "a root bearing poison and wormwood" (Deuteronomy 29:17), in the passage that also speaks of the stubbornness of the heart (29:18; verse 13 here). The bitter fruit of their idolatry is now given back to them. The same words return in 23:15, and the poisoned water in 8:14.

decisions.choice: feeding them ... giving them to drink: the LORD himself sends the suffering
decisions.reason: Food and drink stand for what a person receives in life. The LORD who once fed his people in the wilderness now gives them bitterness to eat and drink.

decisions.choice: bitter wormwood / bitter plants
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "bitter" to tell the reader what wormwood is like; Readable says "bitter plants" for the unfamiliar name.

decisions.choice: mchungu
decisions.reason: "Mchungu" is the bitter herb, the plant whose name means "bitter", for the Hebrew la'anah (wormwood); Readable says "bitter plants" as the English Readable.

source.text: וַהֲפִֽצוֹתִים֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ הֵ֖מָּה וַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will scatter them among the nations which not they have known, they and their fathers, and I will send after them the sword until I have consumed them.

en.L: And I will scatter them among the nations that they have not known, they and their fathers, \q and I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
en.B: I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, \q and I will send the sword to pursue them until I have finished them off.
en.R: I will scatter them among nations that they and their ancestors never knew. \q I will send war after them until I have destroyed them.

es.L: Y los esparciré entre las naciones que no conocieron ni ellos ni sus padres, \q y enviaré tras ellos la espada hasta que los haya acabado.
es.B: Los dispersaré entre naciones que ni ellos ni sus antepasados conocieron, \q y enviaré la espada a perseguirlos hasta acabar con ellos.
es.R: Los dispersaré entre naciones que ni ellos ni sus antepasados conocieron nunca. \q Enviaré la guerra tras ellos hasta destruirlos.

fr.L: Et je les disperserai parmi les nations qu’ils n’ont pas connues, ni eux ni leurs pères, \q et j’enverrai l’épée derrière eux jusqu’à ce que je les aie exterminés.
fr.B: Je les disperserai parmi des nations que ni eux ni leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} n’ont connues, \q et j’enverrai l’épée à leur poursuite jusqu’à ce que j’en aie fini avec eux.
fr.R: Je les disperserai parmi des nations qu’ils n’ont jamais connues, ni eux ni leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. \q J’enverrai la guerre derrière eux jusqu’à ce que je les aie détruits.

sw.L: Nami nitawatawanya kati ya mataifa ambayo hawakuyajua, wao wala baba zao, \q nami nitatuma upanga uwafuatie mpaka nitakapowakomesha.
sw.B: Nitawatawanya kati ya mataifa ambayo wao wala babu zao hawakuyajua, \q nami nitatuma upanga uwafuatilie mpaka nitakapowamaliza.
sw.R: Nitawatawanya kati ya mataifa ambayo wao na babu zao hawakuyajua kamwe. \q Nitatuma vita viwafuatie mpaka nitakapowaangamiza.

decisions.choice: scatter ... among the nations ... send the sword after them: the curses of the covenant
decisions.reason: The words echo the warnings of the law: "I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you" (Leviticus 26:33), and "the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples ... gods which neither you nor your fathers have known" (Deuteronomy 28:64; compare 28:36).

decisions.choice: until I have made an end of them: the threat in its full force
decisions.reason: The verb means to finish, to bring to an end. Elsewhere the LORD says he will not make a full end of his people (4:27; 5:10, 18; 30:11). Here the sentence is stated in its full strength, as the covenant curses state it; the hope of a remnant is not in view in this verse.

decisions.choice: war; destroyed them
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "the sword", as this book does in the list "sword, famine and disease", and "destroyed them" for "made an end of them".

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת וּתְבוֹאֶ֑ינָה וְאֶל־הַחֲכָמ֥וֹת שִׁלְח֖וּ וְתָבֽוֹאנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: consider and call for the mourning women, and let them come; and to the skillful [women] send, and let them come,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; \q and send for the skillful women, that they may come,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Think about what is happening, and call for the mourning women; let them come. \q Send for the women who are skilled in lament; let them come,
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q Think about this! Call for the women whose work is to mourn the dead. Tell them to come. \q Send for the women who know how to sing songs of grief. Tell them to come.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: \q {{plural_you:Consideren|Considerad}}, y {{plural_you:llamen|llamad}} a las plañideras, que vengan; \q y {{plural_you:envíen|enviad}} por las mujeres hábiles, que vengan,
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: \q {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en lo que está pasando, y {{plural_you:llamen|llamad}} a las plañideras; que vengan. \q {{plural_you:Manden|Mandad}} buscar a las mujeres expertas en lamentos; que vengan,
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: \q ¡{{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en esto! {{plural_you:Llamen|Llamad}} a las mujeres cuyo oficio es llorar a los muertos. {{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}} que vengan. \q {{plural_you:Manden|Mandad}} buscar a las mujeres que saben cantar cantos de dolor. {{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}} que vengan.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : \q Soyez attentifs, et appelez les pleureuses, et qu’elles viennent ; \q et envoyez chercher les femmes habiles, et qu’elles viennent,
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : \q Réfléchissez à ce qui arrive, et appelez les pleureuses ; qu’elles viennent ! \q Envoyez chercher les femmes expertes en lamentations ; qu’elles viennent,
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : \q Réfléchissez ! Appelez les femmes dont le métier est de pleurer les morts. Dites-leur de venir. \q Envoyez chercher les femmes qui savent chanter des chants de deuil. Dites-leur de venir.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: \q Fikirini, mkawaite wanawake waombolezaji, waje; \q na mtume kwa wanawake stadi, waje,
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: \q Fikirini yanayotokea, mkawaite wanawake waombolezaji; na waje. \q Tumeni kuwaita wanawake walio stadi wa maombolezo; na waje,
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: \q Fikirini jambo hili! Waiteni wanawake ambao kazi yao ni kuwaombolezea wafu. Waambieni waje. \q Tumeni kuwaita wanawake wanaojua kuimba nyimbo za huzuni. Waambieni waje.

decisions.choice: the mourning women ... the skillful women: women who led the laments at funerals
decisions.reason: In Israel, as among its neighbors, mourning for the dead was led by women who knew the traditional laments and could stir others to weep (Amos 5:16; 2 Chronicles 35:25). "Skillful" is the word for "wise" used of a craft (Exodus 35:25); these women were skilled at their task and were called in when someone died. Now they are summoned to mourn a whole nation.

decisions.choice: consider, and call: the people are addressed
decisions.reason: The commands are plural and spoken to the people. They are to take in what is coming and prepare for a funeral, their own.

decisions.choice: Think about what is happening; whose work is to mourn the dead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "consider" has no object; Balanced and Readable supply one. Readable explains who the mourning women were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "las plañideras"
decisions.reason: The women hired to lead the laments at funerals have their own Spanish name; Readable says what they did, as the English does.

source.text: וּתְמַהֵ֕רְנָה וְתִשֶּׂ֥נָה עָלֵ֖ינוּ נֶ֑הִי וְתֵרַ֤דְנָה עֵינֵ֨ינוּ֙ דִּמְעָ֔ה וְעַפְעַפֵּ֖ינוּ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And let them hurry and raise over us wailing, and let our eyes run down [with] tears, and our eyelids flow [with] water.

en.L: and let them hurry and raise a wailing over us, \q that our eyes may run down with tears \q and our eyelids flow with water.
en.B: and let them hurry and raise a wailing over us, \q so that our eyes overflow with tears \q and water streams from our eyelids.
en.R: Let them hurry and cry out in grief for us. \q Then our eyes will fill with tears, \q and water will pour from our eyelids.

es.L: y que se apresuren y alcen sobre nosotros lamento, \q para que nuestros ojos derramen lágrimas \q y nuestros párpados destilen agua.
es.B: y que se den prisa y alcen un lamento por nosotros, \q para que nuestros ojos se llenen de lágrimas \q y de nuestros párpados corra el agua.
es.R: Que se apresuren y lloren a gritos por nosotros. \q Entonces nuestros ojos se llenarán de lágrimas, \q y el agua correrá de nuestros párpados.

fr.L: et qu’elles se hâtent et qu’elles élèvent sur nous une lamentation, \q et que nos yeux fondent en larmes \q et que nos paupières ruissellent d’eau.
fr.B: qu’elles se hâtent d’élever sur nous une lamentation, \q pour que nos yeux débordent de larmes \q et que l’eau ruisselle de nos paupières.
fr.R: Qu’elles se dépêchent de crier leur douleur pour nous. \q Alors nos yeux se rempliront de larmes, \q et l’eau coulera de nos paupières.

sw.L: na wafanye haraka kupaza maombolezo juu yetu, \q ili macho yetu yatiririke machozi \q na kope zetu zibubujike maji.
sw.B: na wafanye haraka kupaza maombolezo juu yetu, \q ili macho yetu yafurike machozi \q na maji yatiririke kutoka kope zetu.
sw.R: Na wafanye haraka walie kwa huzuni kwa ajili yetu. \q Ndipo macho yetu yatajaa machozi, \q na maji yatamiminika kutoka kope zetu.

decisions.choice: over us: the voice of the people
decisions.reason: The speaker now says "us": the people themselves, or the prophet speaking as one of them. The professional mourners are to start the lament so that everyone else can weep.

decisions.choice: eyes run down with tears: weeping without stopping
decisions.reason: The picture of eyes running with water is a way of saying grief has no end (8:23; 13:17; 14:17; Lamentations 1:16).

decisions.choice: cry out in grief
decisions.reason: Readable says "cry out in grief" for "raise a wailing".

source.text: כִּ֣י ק֥וֹל נְהִ֛י נִשְׁמַ֥ע מִצִּיּ֖וֹן אֵ֣יךְ שֻׁדָּ֑דְנוּ בֹּ֤שְׁנֽוּ מְאֹד֙ כִּֽי־עָזַ֣בְנוּ אָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י הִשְׁלִ֖יכוּ מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: How we are ruined! We are ashamed greatly, for we have left [the] land, for they have cast down our dwellings.

en.L: For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! \q We are greatly ashamed, for we have left the land, \q for they have thrown down our dwellings."
en.B: For the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! \q How deep is our shame! We have had to leave the land, \q because our homes have been torn down."
en.R: Listen! People in Zion are crying loudly: "We are destroyed! \q We are so ashamed! We have had to leave our land. \q Our homes have been torn down."

es.L: Porque una voz de lamento se oye desde Sion: «¡Cómo hemos sido arruinados! \q Estamos muy avergonzados, porque hemos dejado la tierra, \q porque han derribado nuestras moradas».
es.B: Porque se oye un lamento desde Sion: «¡Qué ruina la nuestra! \q ¡Qué vergüenza tan grande! Hemos tenido que dejar la tierra, \q porque han derribado nuestras casas».
es.R: ¡Atención! La gente de Sion llora a gritos: «¡Estamos destruidos! \q ¡Qué vergüenza! Hemos tenido que dejar nuestra tierra. \q Han derribado nuestras casas».

fr.L: Car une voix de lamentation se fait entendre de Sion : « Comme nous sommes dévastés ! \q Nous sommes couverts de honte, car nous avons quitté le pays, \q car ils ont renversé nos demeures. »
fr.B: Car on entend une lamentation depuis Sion : « Comme nous sommes ruinés ! \q Quelle honte pour nous ! Nous avons dû quitter le pays, \q parce que nos maisons ont été abattues. »
fr.R: Écoutez ! Les gens de Sion poussent de grands cris : « Nous sommes détruits ! \q Nous avons tellement honte ! Nous avons dû quitter notre pays. \q Nos maisons ont été démolies. »

sw.L: Kwa maana sauti ya maombolezo inasikika kutoka Sayuni: "Jinsi tulivyoangamizwa! \q Tumeaibika sana, kwa maana tumeiacha nchi, \q kwa maana wamezibomoa nyumba zetu."
sw.B: Kwa maana sauti ya maombolezo inasikika kutoka Sayuni: "Jinsi tulivyoangamia! \q Jinsi aibu yetu ilivyo kuu! Imetubidi kuiacha nchi, \q kwa sababu nyumba zetu zimebomolewa."
sw.R: Sikilizeni! Watu wa Sayuni wanalia kwa sauti kubwa: "Tumeangamia! \q Tuna aibu kubwa sana! Imetubidi kuiacha nchi yetu. \q Nyumba zetu zimebomolewa."

decisions.choice: they have thrown down our dwellings: the enemy has torn the houses down
alternatives: our dwellings have cast us out
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and active with no named subject: "they", the enemy, have thrown down the people's homes. It can also be read with the dwellings as subject: "our dwellings have thrown us out".

decisions.choice: greatly ashamed: utterly disgraced by defeat
decisions.reason: To be put to shame is to have one's hopes collapse in public, as happens to a defeated people (2:36; 20:11). It is more than a feeling of embarrassment.

decisions.choice: we have left the land: exile
decisions.reason: To leave the land is to go into exile, losing the land the LORD gave to the ancestors. The lament mourns this as if it has already happened.

decisions.choice: had to leave; our homes have been torn down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "had to" because the leaving is forced, and put "they have thrown down" as "have been torn down", since the Hebrew names no subject (meaning decision m1). Readable begins "Listen!" to show that the voices are heard.

source.text: כִּֽי־שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה וְתִקַּ֥ח אָזְנְכֶ֖ם דְּבַר־פִּ֑יו וְלַמֵּ֤דְנָה בְנֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ נֶ֔הִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ קִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For hear, women, [the] word of Yahweh, and let your ear receive [the] word of his mouth; and teach your daughters wailing, and [each] woman her neighbor a lament.

en.L: Now hear, you women, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and let your ear receive the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth; \q teach your daughters a wailing, \q and each woman her neighbor a lament.
en.B: Now, you women, listen to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q let your ears take in the word from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. \q Teach your daughters a song of mourning, \q and teach one another a lament.
en.R: Women, listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. \q Pay attention to the words {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks. \q Teach your daughters to sing sad songs. \q Teach one another songs for the dead.

es.L: {{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}}, pues, mujeres, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q y reciba {{plural_you:su oído|vuestro oído}} la palabra de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca; \q {{plural_you:enseñen a sus hijas|enseñad a vuestras hijas}} lamento, \q y cada una a su vecina, endecha.
es.B: Ahora, mujeres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q que {{plural_you:sus oídos|vuestros oídos}} reciban la palabra de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca. \q {{plural_you:Enseñen a sus hijas|Enseñad a vuestras hijas}} un canto de duelo, \q y {{plural_you:enséñense|enseñaos}} unas a otras un lamento.
es.R: Mujeres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q {{plural_you:Presten|Prestad}} atención a las palabras que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice. \q {{plural_you:Enseñen a sus hijas|Enseñad a vuestras hijas}} a cantar cantos tristes. \q {{plural_you:Enséñense|Enseñaos}} unas a otras cantos para los muertos.

fr.L: Écoutez donc, femmes, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q et que votre oreille reçoive la parole de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche ; \q enseignez à vos filles une lamentation, \q et chaque femme à sa voisine un chant funèbre.
fr.B: Maintenant, femmes, écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q que vos oreilles accueillent la parole de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche. \q Enseignez à vos filles un chant de deuil, \q et apprenez-vous les unes aux autres une lamentation.
fr.R: Femmes, écoutez ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Faites attention aux paroles qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prononce. \q Apprenez à vos filles à chanter des chants tristes. \q Apprenez-vous les unes aux autres des chants pour les morts.

sw.L: Basi sikieni, enyi wanawake, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q na masikio yenu yapokee neno la kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}; \q wafundisheni binti zenu maombolezo, \q na kila mwanamke jirani yake wimbo wa kilio.
sw.B: Basi, enyi wanawake, sikilizeni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q masikio yenu yapokee neno kutoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. \q Wafundisheni binti zenu wimbo wa maombolezo, \q na mfundishane wimbo wa kilio.
sw.R: Enyi wanawake, sikilizeni anayosema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Yasikilizeni maneno anayoyasema. \q Wafundisheni binti zenu kuimba nyimbo za huzuni. \q Fundishaneni nyimbo za kuwalilia wafu.

decisions.choice: teach your daughters ... each woman her neighbor: more mourners will be needed
decisions.reason: Laments were learned and handed on, mother to daughter and woman to woman. The dead will be so many (verses 20-21) that the skilled women alone will not be enough; every woman must learn to mourn.

decisions.choice: lament: a funeral song
decisions.reason: This word names a song sung over the dead, often with a short, limping beat (2 Samuel 1:17; the book of Lamentations). The word for "wailing" beside it is a cry of grief.

decisions.choice: now hear ... your ear: women are addressed
decisions.reason: The opening word stresses the call to listen. The commands are addressed to women, while "your ear" uses the form normally used for men; Hebrew often uses that form for a mixed or general group.

decisions.choice: one another
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "one another" for "each woman her neighbor".

source.text: כִּֽי־עָ֤לָה מָ֨וֶת֙ בְּחַלּוֹנֵ֔ינוּ בָּ֖א בְּאַרְמְנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְהַכְרִ֤ית עוֹלָל֙ מִח֔וּץ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מֵרְחֹבֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: For death has come up in our windows, it has entered in our fortresses, to cut off [the] child from [the] street, young men from [the] squares.

en.L: For death has come up through our windows; \q it has entered our fortresses, \q to cut off the child from the street, \q young men from the squares.
en.B: For death has climbed in through our windows \q and entered our strongholds, \q to cut off the children from the streets \q and the young men from the public squares.
en.R: Death has climbed in through our windows. \q It has come into our strong buildings. \q It takes the children from the streets \q and the young men from the town squares.

es.L: Porque la muerte ha subido por nuestras ventanas, \q ha entrado en nuestros palacios, \q para exterminar al niño de la calle, \q a los jóvenes de las plazas.
es.B: Porque la muerte se ha subido por nuestras ventanas \q y ha entrado en nuestras fortalezas, \q para arrancar a los niños de las calles \q y a los jóvenes de las plazas.
es.R: La muerte se ha metido por nuestras ventanas. \q Ha entrado en nuestros edificios fuertes. \q Se lleva a los niños de las calles \q y a los jóvenes de las plazas.

fr.L: Car la mort est montée par nos fenêtres ; \q elle est entrée dans nos palais fortifiés, \q pour retrancher l’enfant de la rue, \q les jeunes gens des places.
fr.B: Car la mort a grimpé par nos fenêtres \q et elle est entrée dans nos forteresses, \q pour faire disparaître les enfants des rues \q et les jeunes gens des places publiques.
fr.R: La mort a grimpé par nos fenêtres. \q Elle est entrée dans nos bâtiments fortifiés. \q Elle emporte les enfants dans les rues \q et les jeunes gens sur les places de la ville.

sw.L: Kwa maana mauti yamepanda kwa madirisha yetu; \q yameingia ngomeni mwetu, \q kumkatilia mbali mtoto barabarani, \q vijana viwanjani.
sw.B: Kwa maana kifo kimepanda na kuingia kupitia madirisha yetu \q na kuingia katika ngome zetu, \q kuwakatilia mbali watoto barabarani \q na vijana katika viwanja vya mji.
sw.R: Kifo kimepanda na kuingia kupitia madirisha yetu. \q Kimeingia katika majengo yetu imara. \q Kinawachukua watoto barabarani \q na vijana katika viwanja vya mji.

decisions.choice: death has come up through our windows: death as an intruder that no wall keeps out
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a thief or raider climbing in where the doors are barred, getting even into the strongest houses. Stories told among Israel's neighbors spoke of Death as a power that devours the living, and the picture may draw on such ideas, but its sense here is plain: no one is safe anywhere.

decisions.choice: children from the street, young men from the squares: the places of daily life
decisions.reason: The streets were where children played and the squares were where young men gathered (Zechariah 8:4-5). Death empties the public places where the city's life and future were most visible.

decisions.choice: fortresses: strong houses, palaces
decisions.reason: The word means a large, fortified building, a palace or stronghold (Amos 3:10-11). Not even the homes of the powerful are safe.

decisions.choice: climbed in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "climbed in" for "come up", which in this picture means climbing up to and through a window.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֗ר כֹּ֚ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽפְלָה֙ נִבְלַ֣ת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּכְעָמִ֛יר מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י הַקֹּצֵ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין מְאַסֵּֽף׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Speak: thus, declares Yahweh: and will fall [the] corpse of humankind like dung on [the] face of the field, and like cut grain from behind the reaper, and there is none gathering.

en.L: Speak thus, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q The corpses of humankind will fall like dung on the open field, \q and like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one gathering [them].
en.B: Say this, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Human corpses will fall like dung on the open field, \q like cut grain left behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.
en.R: Tell them this message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Dead bodies will lie on the open fields like manure. \q They will be like grain that harvesters cut and leave behind, and no one will gather them up.

es.L: Di así, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Caerán los cadáveres de los hombres como estiércol sobre la faz del campo, \q y como gavilla tras el segador, sin que nadie [la] recoja.
es.B: Di esto, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Los cadáveres humanos caerán como estiércol en campo abierto, \q como gavillas que quedan detrás del segador, sin nadie que las recoja.
es.R: Diles este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: \q Los cadáveres quedarán tirados en los campos como abono. \q Serán como el grano que los segadores cortan y dejan atrás, y nadie los recogerá.

fr.L: Parle ainsi, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : \q Les cadavres des {{gender:humains|hommes}} tomberont comme du fumier sur la face des champs, \q et comme la gerbe derrière le moissonneur, et personne ne [les] ramassera.
fr.B: Dis ceci, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : \q Les cadavres humains tomberont comme du fumier en plein champ, \q comme la gerbe laissée derrière le moissonneur, sans personne pour la ramasser.
fr.R: Dis-leur ce message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : \q Les cadavres resteront dans les champs comme du fumier. \q Ils seront comme les épis que les moissonneurs coupent et laissent derrière eux, et personne ne les ramassera.

sw.L: Sema hivi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q Mizoga ya wanadamu itaanguka kama samadi juu ya uso wa shamba, \q na kama mganda nyuma ya mvunaji, wala hakuna mwenye kuikusanya.
sw.B: Sema hivi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q Maiti za wanadamu zitaanguka kama samadi juu ya shamba, \q kama nafaka iliyokatwa ikaachwa nyuma ya mvunaji, bila mtu wa kuikusanya.
sw.R: Waambie ujumbe huu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q Maiti zitalala mashambani kama mbolea. \q Zitakuwa kama nafaka ambayo wavunaji wameikata na kuiacha nyuma, wala hakuna atakayeikusanya.

decisions.choice: speak thus, declares the LORD: a command to the prophet inside the poem
decisions.reason: The LORD breaks in with an order to the prophet to announce what follows. The lament of verses 19-20 is followed by the LORD's own word on the dead.

decisions.choice: like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one gathering: the dead are left unburied
decisions.reason: At harvest the reaper cut the grain with a sickle and left the stalks lying in rows, and others followed to gather them into sheaves. Here the dead lie like those rows, but no one comes to gather them: there is no one left to bury them (8:2; 16:4; 25:33).

decisions.choice: like dung: a picture of utter disgrace
