decisions.reason: To lie unburied like dung on a field was the worst shame a person could suffer (8:2; 16:4; 2 Kings 9:37).

decisions.choice: Tell them this message; manure; harvesters
decisions.reason: Readable puts the command as "Tell them this message" and uses plain words for "dung" and "reaper".

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֤ל חָכָם֙ בְּחָכְמָת֔וֹ וְאַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל הַגִּבּ֖וֹר בִּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ אַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל עָשִׁ֖יר בְּעָשְׁרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: let not boast [the] wise in his wisdom, and let not boast the mighty in his might; let not boast [the] rich in his riches.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Let not the wise boast in {{gender:their|his}} wisdom, and let not the mighty boast in {{gender:their|his}} might; let not the rich boast in {{gender:their|his}} riches.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: The wise must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} wisdom, the strong must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} strength, and the rich must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} wealth.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Wise people should not brag about how wise they are. Strong people should not brag about how strong they are. Rich people should not brag about how rich they are.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: No se gloríe el sabio en su sabiduría, ni se gloríe el valiente en su valentía; no se gloríe el rico en sus riquezas.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Que el sabio no se jacte de su sabiduría, que el fuerte no se jacte de su fuerza, y que el rico no se jacte de su riqueza.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Los sabios no deben presumir de lo sabios que son. Los fuertes no deben presumir de lo fuertes que son. Los ricos no deben presumir de lo ricos que son.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Que le sage ne se vante pas de sa sagesse, et que le fort ne se vante pas de sa force ; que le riche ne se vante pas de sa richesse.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Que le sage ne se vante pas de sa sagesse, que le fort ne se vante pas de sa force, et que le riche ne se vante pas de sa richesse.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Les gens sages ne doivent pas se vanter d’être sages. Les gens forts ne doivent pas se vanter d’être forts. Les gens riches ne doivent pas se vanter d’être riches.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Mwenye hekima asijisifu kwa hekima yake, wala mwenye nguvu asijisifu kwa nguvu zake; tajiri asijisifu kwa utajiri wake.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Mwenye hekima asijivune kwa hekima yake, mwenye nguvu asijivune kwa nguvu zake, wala tajiri asijivune kwa mali yake.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Watu wenye hekima wasijigambe kwa jinsi walivyo na hekima. Watu wenye nguvu wasijigambe kwa jinsi walivyo na nguvu. Matajiri wasijigambe kwa jinsi walivyo matajiri.

decisions.choice: boast: take pride in, rely on as one's glory
decisions.reason: The verb means to praise oneself, to make something one's pride and confidence. What a person boasts in is what they trust to make them secure and important.

decisions.choice: the wise, the mighty, the rich: the things a people trusted
decisions.reason: Wisdom, military strength and wealth were the marks of a successful nation and its leaders. Jeremiah has already shown the wise with no word from the LORD (8:8-9; verse 11 here), and the strong and rich will not be saved by what they have (5:27-28).

decisions.choice: a new saying in prose
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the chapter the text is prose, not poetry. The saying of verses 22-23 answers the question of verse 11: true wisdom is to know the LORD.

decisions.choice: the strong ... strength; wealth / brag
decisions.reason: Balanced says "strong" and "strength" for the warrior's might and "wealth" for riches. Readable says "brag about how wise they are", which says the same thing in plain words.

decisions.choice: "su sabiduría", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" serves for men and women alike, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "le sage ... sa sagesse", no gender span
decisions.reason: French "sa" agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner, so "sa sagesse" says nothing about whether the wise one is a man or a woman; the English gender spans have no French counterpart.

source.text: כִּ֣י אִם־בְּזֹ֞את יִתְהַלֵּ֣ל הַמִּתְהַלֵּ֗ל הַשְׂכֵּל֮ וְיָדֹ֣עַ אוֹתִי֒ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֛סֶד מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־בְאֵ֥לֶּה חָפַ֖צְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But rather in this let boast the [one] boasting: having insight and knowing me, that I [am] Yahweh doing loyal love, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these I delight, declares Yahweh.

en.L: But let the one who boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who does loyal love, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these I delight, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Instead, whoever boasts should boast of this: that they understand and know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who acts with loyal love, justice and righteousness on the earth. For these are what I delight in, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Instead, anyone who wants to brag should brag about this: that they understand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I act with faithful love, justice and righteousness on the earth. These are the things that please {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Mas el que se gloríe, gloríese en esto: en entender{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} y conocer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que hago amor leal, derecho y justicia en la tierra; porque en estas cosas me complazco, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Más bien, quien se gloríe, que se gloríe en esto: en que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entiende y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conoce, en que sabe que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que actúo con amor fiel, derecho y justicia en la tierra. Porque en esto me complazco, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Al contrario, el que quiera presumir, que presuma de esto: de que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entiende y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conoce. De que sabe que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo actúo con amor fiel, justicia y rectitud en la tierra. Estas son las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} agradan, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Mais que celui qui se vante se vante de ceci : d’avoir de l’intelligence et de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, de savoir que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui exerce l’amour loyal, le droit et la justice sur la terre ; car c’est en cela que je prends plaisir, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Que celui qui se vante se vante plutôt de ceci : de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} comprendre et de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, de savoir que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui agit avec amour fidèle, droit et justice sur la terre. Car c’est en cela que je prends plaisir, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Au contraire, que celui qui veut se vanter se vante de ceci : de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} comprendre et de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître. Qu’il sache que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. J’agis avec amour fidèle, avec droit et justice sur la terre. Ce sont ces choses-là qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} plaisent, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Bali yeye ajisifuye na ajisifu kwa hili: kwamba ana ufahamu na kunijua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ya kuwa mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitendaye upendo usiokoma, hukumu na haki duniani; kwa maana katika hayo napendezwa, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Badala yake, anayetaka kujivuna na ajivune kwa hili: kwamba ananielewa na kunijua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ya kuwa mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninayetenda kwa upendo usiokoma, kwa haki na kwa uadilifu duniani. Kwa maana mambo hayo ndiyo ninayoyapenda, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Badala yake, mtu yeyote anayetaka kujigamba na ajigambe kwa hili: kwamba ananielewa na kunijua. Anajua kwamba mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ninatenda kwa upendo usiokoma, kwa haki na kwa uadilifu duniani. Hayo ndiyo mambo yanayonipendeza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: let the one who boasts boast in this: quoted by Paul
decisions.reason: Paul sums up this verse as "The one who boasts must boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31; 2 Corinthians 10:17), setting God's wisdom in Christ against human wisdom, strength and status, as Jeremiah sets knowing the LORD against wisdom, might and riches.

decisions.choice: understanding and knowing me: knowing the LORD for who he is
decisions.reason: The two verbs say "having insight and knowing", without naming a person or a time. To "know" the LORD is to acknowledge him and live in his ways; Jeremiah later says that to do justice for the poor "is to know me" (22:16). It answers verses 2 and 5, where the people refuse to know him.

decisions.choice: loyal love, justice and righteousness: what the LORD does and loves
decisions.reason: Loyal love (*hesed*) is faithful, generous love kept within a covenant. Justice is setting things right, especially for the weak; righteousness is doing what is right by others. The LORD does these "in the earth", among people, and delights in them, so those who know him will do them too (22:3, 15-16).

decisions.choice: loyal love / faithful love
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable put "understanding and knowing me" as "that they understand and know me", and Readable breaks the sentence into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "quien se gloríe, que se gloríe en esto"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets it, the key words Paul quotes in 1 Corinthians 1:31, so the reader can hear the quotation; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: ajisifuye na ajisifu (Literal); ajivune (Balanced); ajigambe (Readable)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line (1 Corinthians 1:31; 2 Corinthians 10:17); Literal keeps the word "kujisifu" so the quotation can be recognized.

decisions.choice: "que celui qui se vante se vante de ceci"
decisions.reason: "Se vanter" is the verb of the French 1 Corinthians 1:31, which quotes this verse, so the reader can recognize it.

decisions.choice: "que celui qui veut se vanter ... qu’il sache"
decisions.reason: French keeps "celui qui ... il", which is already generic, where the English Readable uses "they".

source.text: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וּפָ֣קַדְתִּ֔י עַל־כָּל־מ֖וּל בְּעָרְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: See, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will punish every [one] circumcised in foreskin,

en.L: See, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will punish all who are circumcised in the foreskin,
en.B: The time is coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will bring punishment on all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised,
en.R: The time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will punish everyone who is circumcised only in body.

es.L: He aquí vienen días, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que castigaré a todo circuncidado en el prepucio,
es.B: Vienen días, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que castigaré a todos los que están circuncidados y, sin embargo, siguen incircuncisos,
es.R: Se acerca el tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que castigaré a todos los que están circuncidados solo en el cuerpo.

fr.L: Voici, des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où je punirai tous ceux qui sont circoncis dans le prépuce,
fr.B: Des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où je punirai tous ceux qui sont circoncis et pourtant incirconcis :
fr.R: Un temps vient, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où je punirai tous ceux qui ne sont circoncis que dans leur corps.

sw.L: Tazama, siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapowaadhibu wote waliotahiriwa katika govi,
sw.B: Wakati unakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapowaletea adhabu wote waliotahiriwa lakini hawajatahiriwa,
sw.R: Wakati unakuja, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapomwadhibu kila mtu aliyetahiriwa mwilini tu.

decisions.choice: circumcised in the foreskin: circumcised yet uncircumcised, the outward sign without the reality
decisions.reason: The phrase is a paradox: people who are circumcised and yet still "in foreskin". Verse 25 explains it: the nations are uncircumcised and Israel is uncircumcised in heart, so the outward mark does not protect anyone. The phrase can also be taken as "circumcised and uncircumcised alike", meaning everyone without exception; verse 25 favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: days are coming: a time the LORD will bring
decisions.reason: This formula announces a future act of God, whether of judgment (7:32; 19:6) or of restoration (16:14; 23:5; 31:31).

decisions.choice: punish: visit in judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit, to come and deal with someone; with "on" it means to bring punishment (verse 8).

decisions.choice: circumcised only in body
decisions.reason: Readable puts the paradox in plain words: the people have the mark of circumcision on their bodies, but nothing more (meaning decision m1). Readable ends the sentence here and repeats "I will punish" in verse 25.

source.text: עַל־מִצְרַ֣יִם וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֗ה וְעַל־אֱד֞וֹם וְעַל־בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ וְעַל־מוֹאָ֔ב וְעַל֙ כָּל־קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֔ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֤י כָל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ עֲרֵלִ֔ים וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַרְלֵי־לֵֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: on Egypt and on Judah and on Edom and on [the] sons of Ammon and on Moab and on all [those] clipped [at the] corner who dwell in the wilderness; for all the nations [are] uncircumcised, and all [the] house of Israel [are] uncircumcised of heart.

en.L: on Egypt, and on Judah, and on Edom, and on the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, and on Moab, and on all who are clipped [at the] corners, who live in the wilderness; for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
en.B: Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the hair at their temples and live in the desert. For every one of these nations is uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
en.R: I will punish Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon and Moab. I will punish the desert tribes who cut their hair short at the sides. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the people of Israel are uncircumcised in heart: their hearts are closed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: a Egipto, y a Judá, y a Edom, y a los hijos de Amón, y a Moab, y a todos los que se rapan [las] sienes, que habitan en el desierto; porque todas las naciones son incircuncisas, y toda la casa de Israel es incircuncisa de corazón.
es.B: a Egipto, a Judá, a Edom, a los amonitas, a Moab y a todos los que se rapan las sienes y viven en el desierto. Porque todas estas naciones son incircuncisas, y toda la casa de Israel es incircuncisa de corazón.
es.R: Castigaré a Egipto, a Judá, a Edom, a Amón y a Moab. Castigaré a las tribus del desierto que se cortan el pelo a los lados de la cabeza. Porque todas estas naciones son incircuncisas, y todo el pueblo de Israel es incircunciso de corazón: su corazón está cerrado para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: l’Égypte, et Juda, et Édom, et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Ammon, et Moab, et tous ceux qui se rasent les tempes, qui habitent dans le désert ; car toutes les nations sont incirconcises, et toute la maison d’Israël est incirconcise de cœur.
fr.B: l’Égypte, Juda, Édom, les Ammonites, Moab, et tous ceux qui se taillent les cheveux sur les tempes et habitent le désert. Car toutes ces nations sont incirconcises, et toute la maison d’Israël est incirconcise de cœur.
fr.R: Je punirai l’Égypte, Juda, Édom, Ammon et Moab. Je punirai les tribus du désert qui se coupent les cheveux sur les côtés de la tête. Car toutes ces nations sont incirconcises, et tout le peuple d’Israël est incirconcis de cœur : leur cœur {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est fermé.

sw.L: juu ya Misri, na juu ya Yuda, na juu ya Edomu, na juu ya wana wa Amoni, na juu ya Moabu, na juu ya wote walionyoa [nywele za] pembeni, wakaao nyikani; kwa maana mataifa yote hawajatahiriwa, na nyumba yote ya Israeli hawajatahiriwa moyoni.
sw.B: Misri, Yuda, Edomu, Waamoni, Moabu, na wote wanaonyoa nywele za pembeni mwa vichwa vyao na kuishi jangwani. Kwa maana kila mmoja wa mataifa haya hajatahiriwa, na nyumba yote ya Israeli haijatahiriwa moyoni.
sw.R: Nitaiadhibu Misri, Yuda, Edomu, Amoni na Moabu. Nitayaadhibu makabila ya jangwani yanayokata nywele zao fupi pembeni. Kwa maana mataifa haya yote hayajatahiriwa, na watu wote wa Israeli hawajatahiriwa moyoni: mioyo yao imefungwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.

decisions.choice: Egypt, Edom, Ammon, Moab ... all the nations are uncircumcised: circumcision without covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision was not only Israel's custom: the Egyptians practiced it, and some of Israel's neighbors seem to have done so too. To the LORD it means nothing in itself. Judah is listed among these nations, as one more people with the outward mark and no more.

decisions.choice: clipped at the corners: desert tribes who cut the hair at the sides of the head
alternatives: those who live in the far corners of the desert
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely describes the desert Arab tribes, who cut their hair short at the temples; Jeremiah uses it of them again in 25:23 and 49:32. Israel was told not to cut the hair at the sides of the head (Leviticus 19:27), perhaps because the custom was tied to other worship. The words could also mean "those who live in the far corners" of the desert; either way the same peoples are meant.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised in heart: a heart closed to the LORD
decisions.reason: The law speaks of an uncircumcised heart that must be humbled (Leviticus 26:41) and calls Israel to circumcise the foreskin of their hearts (Deuteronomy 10:16), a work the LORD himself promises to do (Deuteronomy 30:6). Jeremiah gave the same call (4:4). Israel, circumcised in body, is no better than the nations, because its heart is closed to God.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites; I will punish; their hearts are closed to me
decisions.reason: Balanced says "the Ammonites" for "the sons of Ammon". Readable repeats "I will punish" from verse 24 and explains "uncircumcised in heart" as Leviticus 26:41 does at Readable.

decisions.choice: hawajatahiriwa moyoni
decisions.reason: "Uncircumcised in heart" in the words of Deuteronomy 10:16, as at 4:4.

decisions.choice: "incirconcis de cœur"
decisions.reason: The wording of the call to circumcise the heart in 4:4 and Deuteronomy 10:16, kept at every level as the English keeps it.
